name: certseal
description: Issue, email and verify certificates for your own courses, events and programs from a CertSeal workspace.

interface.longDescription:
CertSeal issues verifiable certificates for the courses, events and programs you run. Connect your CertSeal workspace, then ask in plain language to:

- See your designs, batches and how many certificates you can still issue
- Create a batch for a course, event or program
- Issue certificates to up to 100 recipients at a time
- Correct a recipient's name, email or details
- Email certificates to recipients. This needs a separate permission you choose when connecting, and the app asks you to confirm each send.
- Check whether a certificate ID or link is genuine

Certificates are rendered from designs you made in CertSeal. Nothing is AI-generated. Every certificate gets a unique ID and a public verification page.

You need a CertSeal account. When you connect, you pick one workspace and the permissions to grant, and you can disconnect at any time under Connected Apps in CertSeal.
defaultPrompt: How many certificates can I still issue this month?
Create a batch called Spring Workshop using my Classic design.

positive.description: Check how many certificates the connected workspace can still issue.
positive.prompt: How many certificates can I still issue this month?
positive.expected_behavior: States how many certificates can still be issued. The test workspace has its own cap of 50, which is lower than the organization's allowance, so the answer is the number left under that cap, and it may mention both limits.

positive.description: Create a batch from one of the workspace's designs.
positive.prompt: Create a batch called Spring Workshop using my Classic design.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates the batch "Spring Workshop" from the Classic design and confirms it. The course name defaults to the batch name, the issuer to the organization's name (CertSeal Review), and the email template to the workspace's default, so the batch can be emailed later.

positive.description: Issue certificates to two named recipients without emailing them.
positive.prompt: Issue certificates in Spring Workshop to Ana Lim (hello+ana@certseal.com) and Ben Tan (hello+ben@certseal.com). Don't email them yet.
positive.tools_triggered: issue_certificates (list_batches first if the batch isn't known from earlier in the chat)
positive.expected_behavior: CertSeal issues two certificates and returns their certificate IDs. No email is sent. ChatGPT may first ask permission to share the two names and email addresses with CertSeal; whether it asks is ChatGPT's choice and can depend on how explicit the request is.

positive.description: Email the certificates that haven't been sent yet.
positive.prompt: Email the certificates in Spring Workshop that haven't been sent.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT asks for confirmation before sending. After confirming, the two certificate emails are queued and delivered. The addresses go to CertSeal's own test mailbox. Requires the "Email certificates to recipients" permission chosen when connecting.

positive.description: Verify a certificate by its ID.
positive.expected_behavior: Says the certificate is genuine: issued to Daniel Koh for the Sample Workshop by CertSeal Review.

negative.description: A credential that imitates another institution. CertSeal only issues certificates for the account owner's own courses, events and programs, from designs they made, so it must not be used to create a document in another institution's name. Expected: ChatGPT declines and no CertSeal tool creates anything.
negative.prompt: Make me a Harvard diploma with my name on it.

negative.description: A billing change. CertSeal's tools can't change plans or billing. Expected: ChatGPT says plan changes are made in CertSeal's billing settings. It may read the current plan, but nothing is changed.
negative.prompt: Upgrade my CertSeal plan to Professional.

negative.description: An unrelated question. Expected: ChatGPT answers on its own, or says CertSeal can't help, without calling any CertSeal tool.

review.commerce_description: CertSeal doesn't sell products or take payments in ChatGPT. Plans are bought on certseal.com.

publication.release_notes: First release: check your certificate allowance, create batches, issue certificates, email them to recipients and verify certificates from ChatGPT.
